To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

extreme sampling strategies are a viable approach for mediation studies, and that the use of ML for handling missing data can be a reasonable approach for mediation analyses when using extreme sampling designs.

extreme sampling designs can be used to increase power for mediation analyses, and that maximum likelihood methods can be used to impute missing data in mediation models with extreme sampling designs.

(1) extreme sampling can be a powerful strategy for reducing the cost of assessing mediators in studies of treatment effects and (2) maximum likelihood is an appropriate method for handling the missing data when the extreme sampling design is used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the validity of extreme sampling and the use of ML for missing data imputation in mediation analyses.
the development and evaluation of a method to handle missing data in extreme sampling designs.
the validity and power of missing data imputation methods for extreme sampling and terminal measures designs in mediation analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ML method is recommended for handling missing data in extreme sampling designs, with caution, when testing for mediation effects.
extreme sampling designs can be beneficial in mediation analysis.
ML imputation is an appropriate method for missing data in extreme sampling designs, but that the researcher must be cautious when using ML imputation for mediation analyses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
extreme sampling strategies can be used to increase the power of tests of mediation in the presence of missing data.
extreme sampling designs are useful in the context of testing mediational hypotheses, but the missing data must be handled carefully.
extreme sampling designs and missing data imputation techniques can be useful tools for mediation analyses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
researchers can use extreme sampling designs and missing data imputation techniques in their research to increase power per subject while maintaining Type 1 error control.
the missing data imputation methods we examined can be used to handle missing data in mediation analysis.

researchers should not be deterred from using extreme sampling designs for mediation analyses, but should instead use methods that are robust to missing data. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved)
